title: Request for Information - Contract Writing System Recompete
description: Request for Information Contract Writing System Recompete 2099AC27N00004 RFI-DO-27-002 The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to identify capable vendors and commercially available solutions that can support the U.S. Department of the Treasury requirements for a contract writing system as part of the Contract Writing System Recompete. The Government seeks information regarding vendors� technical capabilities, available products and services, hosting, system functionality, integration, and ability to satisfy the attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements. Interested vendors should review the entire Technical Exhibit and identify capabilities, limitations, and potential alternatives. This RFI is solely for market research and acquisition planning and is not a solicitation. This is an RFI for market research purposes, and not a solicitation. 1. SCOPE SUMMARY (See attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements) The Department of the Treasury is conducting market research to identify qualified vendors capable of providing an enterprise contract writing system solution to support Treasury acquisition and procurement operations. Technical Exhibit 1 identifies anticipated functional, technical, operational, security, hosting, integration, and support requirements designated as Mandatory or Value Added. The Government may use information obtained through this RFI to refine requirements and determine an appropriate acquisition strategy for any future solicitation. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gather information from interested vendors regarding their capabilities and potential solutions for a Contract Writing System to support the Department of the Treasury's acquisition and contracting requirements. The incumbent contractor providing the Department's existing Contract Writing System is Unison Software, Inc. II. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The anticipated period of performance for any resulting contract has not been finalized. Additional information regarding the period of performance, implementation schedule, and other acquisition details may be provided in a future solicitation, should one be issued. III. POTENTIAL INDUSTRY DAY / PRODUCT DEMONSTRATIONS The Government may elect to conduct an Industry Day and/or schedule individual vendor demonstrations as part of its market research efforts to better understand available commercial contract writing systems, products, solutions, services, and capabilities relevant to this RFI and the attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements. Interested vendors may be invited to demonstrate their proposed solutions, highlight key features and functionality, and discuss how their offerings could address the Government's operational and technical needs. Participation in any Industry Day or vendor demonstration will be voluntary and at the Government's sole discretion. Additional information regarding scheduling, format, and participation requirements will be provided if the Government determines that such an event would be beneficial. The Government is under no obligation to conduct an Industry Day or vendor demonstrations. Any such activities will be conducted solely for market research and informational purposes and will not constitute a formal evaluation of offers or quotations. Participation or nonparticipation will not guarantee or preclude consideration for, or award of, any future contract. IV. ADDITIONAL DETAILS NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE. A request for more information, or a copy of the solicitation, will not be considered an affirmative response to this Request for Information. Telephone responses or inquiries to this Request for Information will NOT be accepted. Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC) will consider responses received no later than 10:00 AM ET, November 30, 2026, as submitted in writing to chad.gambrill@treasury.gov and paul.white2@treasury.gov. Please include �RFI: 2099AC27N00004, Contract Writing System Recompete- CG/PW� in the subject line. The Government is conducting market research to identify capable vendors and commercially available solutions. Quotations and formal proposals will not be accepted at this time. The Government may, at its discretion, request clarification or additional technical information from responding vendors or conduct discussions associated with a potential Industry Day or vendor demonstration. Qualified contractors must provide the following: 1. The name and location of your company, contact information, and identify your business size and socioeconomic category. Please ensure contact information includes the name of the point of contact, email address, and telephone number should the Government have questions regarding individual responses. 2. The GSA contract or other vehicle your services are available through, including the schedule/GWAC number, NAICS Codes, and applicable SIN. 3. Capability Statement: Responding vendors shall provide a general capabilities statement describing their company, relevant experience, available contract writing system solutions, and technical capabilities. Responses should address the functional, technical, operational, hosting, integration, security, and support requirements identified in Technical Exhibit 1. 4. Technical Exhibit Response: Vendors are requested to complete the attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements. For each applicable requirement, indicate whether the proposed solution meets the requirement in the "Meets (Y/N)" column and provide explanatory information in the "Comments" column, as appropriate. For requirements not fully met, identify limitations, alternatives, or other approaches. Address both Mandatory and Value Added requirements. The following file extensions are not allowable and application materials/data submitted with these extensions cannot be considered: .bat, .cmd, .com, .exe, .pif, .rar, .scr, .vbs, .hta,, .cpl, and .zip files. Microsoft Office compatible documents are acceptable. Additional information regarding this RFI, including any potential Industry Day or vendor demonstrations, may be provided at the Government discretion. This notice does not restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. All firms responding to this notice are advised that their response is not a request that will be considered for contract award. All interested parties are required to respond to any resultant solicitation separately from their response to this notice, should one be issued.

title: Firefox
description: UPDATE: The purpose of Amendment 1 to DARPA-PA-26-137, the Firefox Program Solicitation (PS), is to update the deadlines for OPP submissions and presentations. The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has developed a non-invasive coherent optical system capable of recording neural signals in humans. To expand this foundational technology and enable the development of revolutionary, non-invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), DARPA's Firefox program is soliciting approaches to overcome key technological hurdles: 1) development of components enabling dynamic rastering/scanning of the incoming coherent optical signal to target multiple regions of interest and 2) development of new data processing architectures beyond the digital domain to handle the high data rates and computational burden inherent to scaling the amount of neural data recorded by the optical system. The ultimate goal of the Firefox program is to use these innovations to develop a 100-channel, non-invasive BCI with 50-micron spatial and 100-microsecond temporal resolution.

title: 19WA8026Q0036 - Janitorial services at Embassy office building and Warehouse.
description: Please note this solicitation is not ready to be issued as of this date. The Embassy of the United States in Windhoek will launch the solicitation on the SAM.gov website when it is available. The U.S. Embassy in Windhoek hereby provides the following pre-solicitation notice in respect of the issuance of a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for: Janitorial/cleaning services at the U.S. Embassy Office building and General services warehouse in Windhoek, Namibia. The Contractor shall perform janitorial services in all designated spaces including, but not limited to halls, offices, restrooms, work areas, entrance ways, lobbies, storage areas, elevators, and stairways. The anticipated performance period is for a base year, with four one-year option periods, if exercised by the Government. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered. The U.S. Government may award the contract, based on the initial offer, without any discussions. The resultant contract will be a fixed priced type of contract for its duration. The Government is planning a pre-quotation conference and the date for this conference will be in the solicitation. All contractors must be registered in the SAM (System for Award Management) Database https://www.sam.gov prior to submitting an offer pursuant to FAR provision 52.204-7. Therefore, prospective offerors are encouraged to register prior to the submittal of quotations/proposals. This opportunity is subject to 52.229-12 - Tax on Certain Foreign Procurements (FEB 2021) Electronic Submission/Responses: This opportunity allows for electronic responses. Please submit your offer prior to the response date and time. Please ensure your email with your offer does not exceed 15 MB, if it does then you might have to send more than one email. Alternatively, offers may be submitted at the US Embassy offices at the following address: 38 Metje Street, Klein Windhoek, Windhoek, Namibia.

title: NWI Offsite Pathology Services
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Nebraska-Western Iowa Health Care System , has a requirement for medical laboratory, pathology and testing analysis services. The Contractor shall be responsible for performing pre-analytic processing as defined in its laboratory manual, analysis, and reporting of analytical results and interpretation for clinical and anatomical pathology specimens as requested by participating facilities (listed below) during the contract period. The contractor shall provide Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Services, on a scheduled basis, in accordance with the specifications, terms and conditions herein. VA will be responsible for specimen collection, preparation, grossing (with the exception of, cytology specimens); global surgical pathology cases would require grossing by the contractor. The VA will accession histology and cytology cases, VistA accessioning, preservation and storage of final slides and blocks. All slides and blocks must be returned to the VA for permanent storage. NOTE: The Solicitation number in the announcement 36C26326R0063 was entered incorrectly, however, cannot be changed. The correct solicitation number is 36C26326Q0727. This number has been reconciled throughout the documents.

title: Progressive Design-Build (PDB) - USSF Integration Facility F/10852 at WPAFB
description: SPECIAL NOTICE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is issuing this special notice to announce an upcoming competition for a design and construction solicitation for the US Space Force Integration Facility, F/10852 using Progressive Design-Build under 10 USC �2808a Other Transaction Authority for Construction. This notice is for informational and planning purposes to allow interested parties to prepare for and provide feedback prior to the official solicitation release. I. INDUSTRY DAY USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 03 December 2026 at 0900 Eastern Time to provide an overview of the project, acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and proposed PDB under an OT (non-FAR-based) framework. A notional acquisition schedule will be shared. Interested parties are encouraged to ask questions and provide input. General questions will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and are for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future RFQ. Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of RFQ. II. LOCATION Industry Day Presentation location: Hope Hotel, 10823 Chidlaw Rd # A, Dayton, OH 45433 III. PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: US Space Force Integration Facility, F/10852 Location: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), OH NAICS Code: 236220 Total Program Funding: $394,000,000.00 IV. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The USSF Integration Facility is a newly programmed mission at Wright-Patterson Air Force WPAFB, Ohio. It serves as a highly classified and secured contiguous operations area to enable Director for National Intelligence (DNI) and United States Space Force (USSF) directed and endorsed missions in areas of the highest national security, housing intelligence analysis and production for new and expanded all-source means that enable near-real-time capabilities. The facility supports the intelligence needs of the Defense Intelligence Enterprise, USSF, joint warfighters, policymakers, and acquisition professionals, driving intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) for space domain operations including detection, characterization, and targeting of adversary space capabilities. The adjacent existing facility, Building F/10854, will remain fully occupied and uninterrupted, maintaining 24/7 business operations and ICD 705 security accreditation throughout construction, requiring strict utility, access, physical security, and logistical phasing constraints. Construction is broken into distinct agreement phases under the Progressive Design-Build (PDB) framework. Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): This Phase is structured to collaboratively advance the facility design from initial concepts to 65% design maturity, perform detailed constructability reviews, conduct transparent open-book cost estimating, identify and mitigate complex interface risks, and validate the overall space programming. Pre-construction services will establish a baseline cost and allow for early design and potential separate authorization of long-lead procurement items. Phase 2 (Final Design and Construction): This Phase will include the completion of final design documents (95% and 100% Certified Final), fast-tracking capabilities, and all physical construction activities, including structural, interior finishes, specialized secure Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) fit-out, redundant systems commissioning, and final security accreditation. Phase 2 will also include comprehensive site work, utility distribution integration, and connection into the active Building F/10854. Phase 2 covers construction of the multi-floor, approximately 333,700 SF secure USSF Integration Facility, including the physical connection to active Building F/10854, the integration of high-efficiency HVAC networks, a backup generator facility, high-security electrical switchgear, and the buildout of specialized SCIF and SAP compartments. The Government will use available concept design information, programmed requirements, and initial planning data as the initial technical baseline. During Phase 1, the selected Design-Builder will validate the baseline and may recommend refinements; any material deviation from the Government�s baseline will require Government review and approval. The scope generally encompasses the following critical lines of effort: Critical Infrastructure and Utilities: Installation of high-efficiency mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems designed for 24/7 continuous operation, electrical tie-ins to centralized utilities, backup generator integration (7,500 KW), Lightning Protection Systems (LPS), and addressable fire protection networks. Secure Facilities: Turnkey design, construction, and Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) accreditation of highly classified Special Access Program (SAP) SCIF spaces built to stringent ICD 705, IC Tech Spec, and Telecommunictaions Electronics Material Protected from Emanating Spurious Tranmission (TEMPEST) shielding standards to ensure complete physical, visual, and acoustic isolation. New Construction, Envelope, and Physical Connection: Construction of a new structural frame with metal panels and pre-cast exterior walls, establishing a secure thermal wall envelope, executing the physical and utility connection to adjacent operational Building F/10854, and conducting all associated site work, paving, and access control infrastructure. V. ACQUISITION STRATEGY - PRE-AWARD The USACE will use a streamlined competitive selection process: Step 1 �RFQ: Interested parties will submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ). Following evaluation of the qualification packages, the Government intends to short-list a target of three (3) of the highest qualified Design-Builders to proceed to Step 2. Step 2 � Pitches: Selected Companies will participate in pitch presentations. One company will be selected as the Design-Build team for award of the initial design and preconstruction services with a modification for design completion and construction award. Step 3 � Exclusive Negotiation: Based on pitch evaluations, the Government will select one Design-Builder to enter exclusive negotiations. VI. ACQUSITION STRATEGY � AWARD The agreement will be awarded to the most qualified Progressive Design-Build Entity (PDBE) to provide design development, preconstruction services, and construction. Post-award Phase 1 of PDB includes Design and Pre-construction services and Post-award Phase 2 includes the final design and construction. The agreement will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). The FFP for successive design and construction milestones will be agreed to as the design progresses and funds are available. VII. VIRTUAL PARTICIPATION OPPORTUNITY: For those who are unable to attend the Industry Day event in person, the Louisville District will also make the event available via Microsoft Teams. The details related to the MS Teams event are provided below: Microsoft Teams Meeting Join: https://dod.teams.microsoft.us/meet/993610255621?p=yaQ28DL3lmCC9Nap5C Meeting ID: 993 610 255 621 Passcode: Y6sB764r VIII. KEY SECURITY REQUIREMENTS This project will require the selected contractor and its subcontractor(s) to process, store, or transmit CUI and Federal Contract Information (FCI). In accordance with the CMMC program (32 CFR part 170) and USACE policy (including Alert 26-HQ-010, Rev1), CMMC Level 2 (Self) will be a mandatory prerequisite prior to award. Offerors must have an active SAM registration and a current, verified BASIC confidence level assessment (or higher) posted in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) in accordance with NIST SP 800-171.
